bloques.titulo: Purpose with identical subject: um-zu versus damit
texto: 1. **um … zu + Infinitiv**: It is used when the subject of the main action and that of the final clause is exactly the same person or entity: **Ich lerne Deutsch, um in Berlin zu studieren** (I study German to study me in Berlin). The **um** particle is located at the beginning of the final group (after coma) and **zu + Infinitiv** is located at the end end.

2. **damit**: If the subjects of both sentences are different, it is mandatory to use **damit** with a complete subordinate: **Ich erkläre es langsam, damit du mich verstehst** (I explain for you to understand).
3. **Separables en final**: If the final infinitive is separable, **zu** intersperses: **um mich vorzubereiten** (to prepare me); **um mich auszuruhen** (to rest).

filas: Er spart, um ein Haus zu bauen.
Er spart, damit seine Kinder studieren.
Sie reist früh an, um sich auszuruhen.

frases.de: Warum nimmst du an dem Intensivkurs teil?
frases.es: ¿Por qué participas en el curso intensivo?
frases.en: Why are you taking part in the intensive course?

frases.de: Ich lerne fleißig, um mich auf den Auslandseinsatz vorzubereiten.
frases.es: Estudio con constancia para prepararme para la misión en el extranjero.
frases.en: I'm constantly studying to prepare for the mission abroad.
analisis: um mich auf den Auslandseinsatz vorzubereiten
to prepare for the mission abroad

frases.de: Fliegst du schon am Sonntag nach London?
frases.en: You fly to London on Sunday?

frases.de: Ja, ich reise früh an, um mich vor dem ersten Treffen auszuruhen.
frases.es: Sí, viajo temprano para descansar antes de la primera reunión.
frases.en: Yeah, I travel early to rest before the first meeting.
analisis: um mich vor dem ersten Treffen auszuruhen
to rest before the first meeting

bloques.pregunta: In what circumstances is it OBLIGATORY to use «um … zu» instead of a «damit» subordinate?

opciones.texto: When the subject of the main action and of the purpose is exactly the same
opciones.explicacion: «um … zu» is the infinitive structure of the subject's identity.

opciones.texto: When the two subjects are people completely different from different departments
opciones.explicacion: If the subjects are different, «damit» must be used.

opciones.texto: Only when the action takes place during the weekend
opciones.explicacion: Temporary circumstances do not determine the syntactic alternation between end connectors.

bloques.pregunta: What final connector should be used in «Ich leihe dir das Buch, ___ du dich informieren kannst»?

opciones.texto: «damit», because the subject of the first sentence (ich) is different from the subject of the second sentence (du)
opciones.explicacion: The disparity of subjects requires subordinated with «damit» conjunction.

opciones.texto: «um … zu», because both actions are related to the same book
opciones.explicacion: The thematic reference does not matter; the syntactic rule serves the grammatical subject.

opciones.texto: «weil», because it expresses the reason for the loan
opciones.explicacion: «weil» would introduce a cause in the past or present, not the purpose of the action.

bloques.frase: Er lernt jeden Tag fleißig Deutsch, ___ in Deutschland arbeiten zu können.

opciones.explicacion: With final infinitive («arbeiten zu können») and same subject, the required connector is «um».
«damit» would require a conjugated subject («damit er in Deutschland arbeiten kann») prayer.
It is a causal connector that expresses the reason or why, not the final objective.

bloques.frase: Ich gebe dir meine Handynummer, ___ du mich jederzeit anrufen kannst.

opciones.explicacion: There are two different subjects («ich» in the main, «du» in the subordinate), which forces you to use «damit».
With two different subjects you cannot use the construction of infinitive with «um».
It would mean «without you can call me», reversing cooperative sense.

bloques.pregunta: What was the target of the early morning?
bloques.frase: Wir sind extra früh aufgestanden, um den ersten Zug nicht zu verpassen.

opciones.texto: Don't lose the first railway convoy in the morning.
opciones.explicacion: «um ... nicht zu verpassen» expresses the preventive purpose with the same subject.

opciones.texto: Have a quiet breakfast at the central station cafeteria.
opciones.explicacion: It does not appear in the phrase; the express objective was not to miss the train.

opciones.texto: Buy the train tickets in the locker for the whole family.
opciones.explicacion: The phrase points out as an explicit goal not to miss the train («nicht zu verpassen»).

bloques.frase: Sie macht sich viele Notizen, ___ nichts Wichtiges zu vergessen.

opciones.explicacion: «um ... zu vergessen» expresses the goal of not forgetting anything with the same subject.
With direct infinitive you cannot head the «damit» clause.
It would mean «instead of not forgetting anything», no logical sense.

bloques.explicacion: subject + verb spare + um + zu reisen at the end.

intro: The final prayers indicate the objective of an action and are formulated with «um … zu» when the subject acting and the one pursuing the end match.
